findings.check: Uncovered code: every exported function of app/public/js against app/test (the demo receipt of REQ-111; look description 8.4, decision 0083 item 8)
findings.title: The date on the demo receipt (astanaDate, a fixed UTC+5 shift) is checked by no test, and a comment says that a test imports it
findings.where: app/public/js/pages/demo.js lines 142 and 189-193 (ASTANA_MS, astanaDate), line 994 (the receipt header), line 1313 (the comment); app/test (no reference)
findings.evidence: grep -rnE 'astanaDate|ASTANA|pages/demo\.js' app/test gives only the string '/js/pages/demo.js' in unit/public-pages.test.js (script-tag rules): no import of demo.js and no name astanaDate under app/test; grep -rnE 'rc-h|\bnum\b' app/test finds no reading of the receipt date in the e2e files. The comment at demo.js:1313 says 'in Node (a test that imports the module for astanaDate) nothing starts', but no such test exists. docs/design/V1-public-look.md lines 103 and 823 fix the date as dd.mm.yyyy in Astana time, UTC+5.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test that imports astanaDate from app/public/js/pages/demo.js (the module starts nothing in Node) and checks the format dd.mm.yyyy, the day border (19:00 UTC gives the next day, 18:59 UTC the same day) and the year border; or let LD-6 read the receipt header and compare it with the page clock shifted by five hours. If no test is wanted, correct the comment. The function is small and may be right: the point is that no test would show a change. A change of app/test needs the owner's rule on guard tests (REQ-113 criterion 13 names two test files for the current run).

findings.title: Eight int tests assert a wall-clock upper bound (3 000, 5 000 or 15 000 ms)
findings.where: app/test/int/db-down.test.js:42-52 (15 000 ms, the bound of REQ-108 criterion 15), health.test.js:75-79, 101-103 and 163-165 (5 000), node-main.test.js:99-103 (5 000), selfcheck.test.js:115-118 (3 000) and 211-215 (5 000)
findings.evidence: grep -rnE 'Date\.now' app/test/int prints `assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 5000)` and the like at the lines above; the four app runs read show no failure of them
findings.recommendation: Keep the 15 000 ms bound of criterion 15 (the requirement names it). For the others, if a runner ever shows a red there, raise the bound or assert the cause (the timeout constant of the code) instead of the elapsed time. No change is due while the records are green; this is a reason to check, not a failing test.
